entries.rule: Track = model_id x member drug x route; opener untested at model_first_use_year
entries.note: de Vrij 2008 (PMID 18571098, epub 25 Apr 2008) quote verbatim. Fenobam is a member; the track's patient comparison (index 2) is oral fenobam, so drug fenobam, route oral, unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: drug/route = the patients compared; same + source_calls_it partial
entries.note: Berry-Kravis 2009 (PMID 19126569, epub 6 Jan 2009) quote verbatim; 'a single oral dose of 50-150 mg of fenobam' in 12 FXS adults. Drug fenobam, oral, unselected and year 2009 confirmed.

entries.rule: Dose: untested/no_prediction when the model stated no exposure, occupancy or margin; rule 6 opening year
entries.note: Yan 2005 (PMID 16054174, epub 27 Jul 2005) quote verbatim; mg/kg MPEP only, no human target. Untested/no_prediction, year 2005, model_first_use_year 2005, mavoglurant oral unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: Rule 6: cell opens at model_first_use_year with status untested
entries.note: Yan 2005 quote verbatim; earliest Fmr1 KO rescue by mGluR5 blockade (Jul 2005). Opener untested 2005, mavoglurant oral (NCT00718341), unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: contra: primary endpoint failed; paired comparison names model side in model_src
entries.note: Jacquemont 2011 (PMID 21209411) quote verbatim; ABC-C primary missed. model_src Yan 2005 precedes trial, prospective. patient_trials mavoglurant only; drug mavoglurant, oral, unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: Safety is per drug; untested_reason unpublished; species cannot show hallucination
entries.note: Youssef 2017 quote verbatim (psychiatric AEs incl. hallucinations/psychosis on basimglurant) in oral-dosed FXS patients; drug basimglurant correct. Proxy year 2008 holds: basimglurant's NCT00809562 posted 2008-12-17. Tox unpublished; untested stands.

entries.rule: Rule 6 opener; drug = member the track is run for
entries.note: McBride 2005 (PMID 15748850, Mar 2005) quote verbatim. Fly-track opener for mavoglurant, oral, consistent with index 4; untested 2005 confirmed.

entries.rule: contra on primary endpoint; drug/route = patients compared
entries.note: Jacquemont 2011 quote verbatim; oral mavoglurant missed ABC-C primary. Fly prediction 2005 is prospective. patient_trials mavoglurant only; drug mavoglurant, oral, unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: Separate track per member drug; opener untested at model_first_use_year (rule 6)
entries.note: Yan 2005 quote verbatim. Basimglurant not tested in Fmr1 KO mice, so sibling-MPEP opener (product_in_model false) is right; untested 2005, basimglurant oral, unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: contra on primary endpoint; rule 6 year = earliest public date
entries.note: Youssef 2017 (PMID 28816242, epub 17 Aug 2017) quote verbatim; ADAMS primary missed. NCT01517698 completed Apr 2014, no posted results; Roche Sept 2014 letter (quoted in draft, not re-fetched) gives 2014. Basimglurant oral unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: Separate track per member drug; opener untested at model_first_use_year
entries.note: McBride 2005 quote verbatim; flies dosed with non-member antagonists, product_in_model false. Basimglurant fly opener untested 2005, oral, unselected confirmed.

entries.rule: contra on primary endpoint; rule 6 year = earliest public date
entries.note: Same FragXis comparison as index 6: Youssef 2017 quote verbatim, ADAMS primary missed; public Sept 2014 via Roche letter. Fly prediction 2005 prospective. contra 2014, basimglurant oral, unselected confirmed.

missing: FXLEARN primary paper, Berry-Kravis 2023 JCI (doi:10.1172/jci171723, NCT02920892): primary WCS endpoint not different from placebo in 3-6 year olds; states 'Despite the large body of evidence supporting use of mGluR5 NAMs in animal models of FXS, this study suggests that this mechanism of action does not translate' (comparison_stated true, tier 1). Should replace the 2024 biomarker paper as the NCT02920892 source and could be the stated-comparison entry on the efficacy track.

Yan 2005 Neuropharmacology (doi:10.1016/j.neuropharm.2005.06.004): MPEP rescued audiogenic seizures and open-field behaviour in Fmr1 KO mice; earliest use of the efficacy/dose model (opening year 2005, not 2008). It also reports a Fragile X-specific tolerance at high mGluR5 antagonist doses.

Drosophila dfmr1 model, McBride 2005 Neuron (doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2005.01.038): MPEP rescued courtship, synaptic plasticity and mushroom body defects; a separate animal system with no track (untested on its own track, or opening proxy).

Dolen 2007 Neuron (doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2007.12.001): genetic Grm5 halving corrected multiple Fmr1 KO phenotypes; the founding mGluR-theory model the trials cite; same mouse system, belongs in the efficacy track's opening evidence.

Human [11C]-ABP688 PET occupancy of mavoglurant in healthy volunteers (doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2021.117785, PMID 33545349): direct engagement readout (27-85% occupancy at 25-400 mg) that 'served to guide the dosing'; no model-stated occupancy target found to pair it with, but it is the class's direct human engagement datum and the draft does not mention it.
rule_questions: The same Fmr1 KO mouse (same de Vrij 2008 paper) carries model_id fmr1-ko-mouse-ppi in engagement and fmr1-ko-mouse-behaviour in dose/efficacy. The brief says one system keeps one slug in every cell; is a readout-specific slug (PPI as the engagement readout) a separate system or a split?

Is a circuit/behavioural readout like PPI admissible as an 'engagement' PD readout at all (readout_tier downstream), when the class has a direct human readout (PET occupancy) that no model stated a target for?

Should efficacy pairings use only member-drug mouse data (mavoglurant Levenga Feb 2011, one month after Jacquemont Jan 2011) or is sibling MPEP data acceptable for the first contra? The draft uses MPEP with product_in_model false; the brief allows it, but the member's own model postdating the trial by one month is not addressed.

dfmr1-drosophila track: Drosophila has no mGluR5 ortholog (its single mGluR, DmGluRA, is group II/III-like), so the fly rescue by MPEP and other mGluR antagonists does not test the class target. Does a model lacking the class target count as a track for an mGluR5 NAM class, or only as a sibling-target model outside the context?
